title: The Chip War Comes To Southeast Asia
text:
The Chip War Comes To Southeast Asia

Tom Miller

Gavekal Research | 8 Oct 2026

In July, the White House fired a warning shot in the artificial-intelligence arms race with China. It accused Chinese startup Moonshot AI of training its models using Nvidia’s most advanced chips, hosted in data centers in Thailand. This legal workaround enabled Moonshot to bypass strict US controls on chip exports to China.Washington is now moving to close the loophole that allows Chinese AI labs to rent access to restricted chips in third countries. The loophole is global, but Southeast Asia is the most important battleground because of its huge data-center buildout and economic ties to both powers. A crackdown could take some of the heat out of the region’s multi-billion-dollar digital investment boom, damaging an important driver of growth. It is the latest in a series of challenges to Southeast Asia’s long-held policy of hedging between the superpowers (see Southeast Asia Plays Both Sides In The US-China Rivalry). Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia all want to be neutral digital hubs. Washington wants them to pick sides.
